text:
Joel Eriksson Ek gave Minnesota a scare on Nov. 12, leaving the win in Toronto after a collision, but he was back for Saturday's 6-2 win over Boston. The Wild have won eight of their last ten, and he is a big part of how they do it.

Minnesota takes 57.8% of the shot attempts and 56.9% of the expected goals with him at five on five, well above its rate without him. He has 66 shots and 11.27 expected goals (expected goals measure chance quality), among the heaviest chance totals on the team. He has six goals. That 5.3-goal gap is the biggest reason to like his season more than his stat line. Goals tend to follow chances.

Two things to watch. He has gone five games without a goal, and his minutes over the last ten are down more than two a night, partly the Toronto exit. And a note of caution the other way: Evolving-Hockey said his results ran ahead of his chances last season. This year it is reversed. He still draws the other team's best, 98th percentile competition last season, and he still has 17 points in 22 games, seven on the power play.
headline: Eriksson Ek is owed some goals
